Page summary pointing to the core reference.
Section heading.
A site declares a small fixed set of concepts, typically Posts and Pages.
Concepts are declared through the adapter's content map.
Each concept is a directory of markdown files plus a fieldset built with defineFieldset.
The fieldset draws on fifteen named field builders.
The fieldset is the single source for the form, the validator, and the inferred type.
A concept is not a generic collection type.
A field type the builders lack is a gap to raise, not a local workaround.
Pointer to declaring your own concept.
A container inside a container throws at declaration, and an array's item must be a leaf.
An object holds only leaves, an array holds a leaf or flat object, and a reference inside an object throws.
A field key never contains a dot, since a dotted path addresses a nested field.
Section heading.
An entry's id is its filename minus .md, with no separate slug codec.
A dated concept adds a leading date to the filename.
The URL slug strips only that leading date prefix.
Renaming changes the filename through a real git operation, not a metadata flip.
The rename operation happens on the holding branch.
An entry's date comes from its own frontmatter, so a dated permalink makes date required.
Section heading.
routing is one of three shorthands: feed, page, or embedded.
page is the default routing.
An embedded concept has no public URL but its entries stay editable.
Section heading.
The save action runs the fieldset validator before any commit and bounces field-keyed errors.
A behavior.validate that throws is caught and the field treated as valid.
Pointer to the debug page.
Section heading.
Entries are read directly from git; the committed manifest serves the rest of the content graph.
The manifest has one row per entry carrying identity, routing, links, reference edges, tags, includes.
A build regenerates and verifies the manifest.
A save patches the manifest entry in the same commit as the content change.
Pointer to the data tiers page.
Section heading.
A reference field holds a typed concept and id pointer and the manifest carries both edge sides.
Pointer to linking content across entries.
Fragments are declared under the reserved fragments key and spliced in with include.
A fragment has no permalink and reaches a reader only through an including entry.
